card.title: 158th BUSHMASTERS
card.text: When a unit is fully repaired, distribute the damage repaired between random enemies.
card.flavorText: The 158th Regiment, initially part of the 45th Division, played a significant role in various operations during WWII. After the US entered the war in 1941, the unit was sent to the Panama Canal Zone where it did security operations and jungle patrols, from which they were given the nickname "Bushmasters" after the venomous snake inhabiting the jungle. In 1942, the 158th Regiment was chosen to create and train a jungle platoon, which led to the prioritization of jungle warfare training. In 1943, the Bushmasters arrived in Australia and later moved to New Guinea, where they participated in Operation Chronicle to establish an airfield on Kiriwina Island. Later elements of the regiment were deployed to Arawe, New Britain, and later to Finschhafen, where it was redesignated as the 158th Regimental Combat Team. The team joined Task Force Tornado and engaged in intense battles with the Japanese in New Guinea. The regimental combat team fought in the Battle of Noemfoor and the invasion of Luzon in the Philippines. Lastly the Bushmasters then invaded the Bicol Peninsula in the Philippines in April 1945. The Bushmasters then participated in the occupation of Japan before being inactivated in January 1946. General MacArthur commended the Bushmasters, stating that no greater combat team had ever deployed for battle.
